```{r}
#| label: load-data

# Small tidy files produced by R/02_clean_data.R live in data/
# example <- read_csv(here("posts", "globe-csi-comparison", "data", "example.csv"))

# Crime Severity Index and violent CSI, 1998 on, for Canada, Ontario and
# Waterloo Region (labelled "Region", cwr_region). One row per place per year.
csi_comparison <- read_csv(
  here("posts", "globe-csi-comparison", "data", "csi_comparison.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Waterloo Region incident rates per 100,000 people, with each rate indexed to
# its base year (100 = the base-year rate). One row per offence per year.
assaults_indexed <- read_csv(
  here("posts", "globe-csi-comparison", "data", "wrps_assaults_indexed.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
sexual_offences_indexed <- read_csv(
  here("posts", "globe-csi-comparison", "data", "wrps_sexual_offences_indexed.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
```

## First finding as a plain-language heading

<!-- One or two paragraphs, then one chart. -->

```{r}
#| label: csi

# Replicates the Globe and Mail's first chart (the Crime Severity Index for
# Canada) and adds Ontario and Waterloo Region. Built from the ggline template.
# Interactive: hovering near a line shows the place, year and index value.

# Colours carry the house meanings: Waterloo Region is the focus (blue), Canada
# the main comparison (red), Ontario context (grey). The Region is labelled
# with the house stock label, cwr_region ("Region").
csi_groups <- c("Canada", "Ontario", cwr_region)
csi_colours <- set_names(c(habsred, cowboysilver, dodgerblue), csi_groups)

# The tooltip text is built once per row, here, rather than in the ggplot call.
# ggiraph shows it as HTML, so <b> and <br> work. hover_id ties the two
# invisible point layers below together (see cwr_interactive() in theme_cwr.R).
csi_plot_data <- csi_comparison |>
  mutate(
    region = factor(region, levels = csi_groups),
    hover_id = str_glue("{region}-{year}"),
    csi_tooltip = str_glue("<b>{region}</b><br>{year}<br>CSI: {label_number(accuracy = 0.1)(csi)}"),
    csi_violent_tooltip = str_glue("<b>{region}</b><br>{year}<br>Violent CSI: {label_number(accuracy = 0.1)(csi_violent)}")
  )

# Set x min and max
x_min <- csi_plot_data |> pull(year) |> min()
x_max <- csi_plot_data |> pull(year) |> max()

# Line-name labels. cwr_line_labels() sets each one's height from its own
# line: `at` is the year it is centred on, where that line has clear space,
# and `side` puts it just above or below the line there.
label_data <- cwr_line_labels(
  csi_plot_data, x = year, y = csi, group = region,
  at = set_names(c(2004, 2014, 2002), csi_groups),
  side = set_names(c("above", "below", "below"), csi_groups),
  bold = cwr_region
)

p <- ggplot(csi_plot_data, aes(x = year, y = csi, colour = region)) +

  geom_label(
    data = label_data,
    aes(x = x, y = y, label = label, fontface = fontface, vjust = vjust),
    colour = "grey30",
    fill = "white",
    linewidth = 0,
    size = 3.2,
    hjust = 0.5,     # centred on the year given in `at`
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +

  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +

  # Hover targets: large invisible squares that catch the mouse anywhere near
  # a line and carry the tooltip...
  geom_point_interactive(
    aes(tooltip = csi_tooltip, data_id = hover_id),
    shape = 15, size = 7, alpha = 0
  ) +
  # ...and small invisible dots that appear on hover to mark the year.
  geom_point_interactive(aes(data_id = hover_id), size = 2.5, alpha = 0) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(2000, x_max, 5),
    labels = label_number(big.mark = "", scale = 1, suffix = ""),
    minor_breaks = seq(x_min, x_max, 1),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.05)),
    position = "bottom"
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(45, NA),   # room under the lowest line for a label
    position = "right",
    labels = label_number(big.mark = ",", scale = 1, suffix = ""),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
  ) +

  scale_colour_manual(
    values = csi_colours,
    guide = "none"
  ) +

  guides(x = guide_axis(minor.ticks = TRUE)) +

  # Right-axis label positioning: sit labels above gridlines
  theme(
    axis.text.y.right = element_text(
      size = rel(1),
      hjust = 1.0,
      vjust = -0.5,
      margin = margin(r = 12, l = -20)
    )
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Title: the finding, in one line",
    subtitle = "Subtitle: what is measured, for whom, and when<br>",
    caption = cwr_caption(c("Statistics Canada Table 35-10-0026-01", "Table 35-10-0188-01"))
  )

cwr_interactive(
  p, "fig-csi",
  alt = paste(
    "Line chart of the Crime Severity Index from", x_min, "to", x_max,
    "for Canada, Ontario and Waterloo Region. All three fell from the late",
    "1990s to a low around 2014 and have risen part of the way back since.",
    "Canada is highest throughout, Ontario lowest, and Waterloo Region sits",
    "between them, closer to Ontario."
  ),
  height = 5, phone_height = 4.5,
  phone = list(scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(2000, x_max, 10),
    minor_breaks = seq(x_min, x_max, 1),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.05))
  ))
)
```

```{r}
#| label: assaults

# Replicates the Globe and Mail's third chart (assault rates for Canada,
# indexed) for Waterloo Region instead. Five offences share one axis because
# each rate is indexed: 100 is its rate in the base year. Five long offence
# names would collide as direct labels, so this chart uses a legend above the
# panel (style rule 3's exception). Hover shows the offence, year, index and
# the underlying rate.

assault_groups <- c(
  "Assault with a weapon or causing bodily harm",
  "Assaults against a peace officer",
  "Aggravated assault",
  "Assault",
  "Other assaults"
)
# Reds for the two offences that have risen most, blues for the level 1 and
# 3 assaults, grey for the catch-all.
assault_colours <- set_names(
  c(habsred, habsred50, dodgerblue, dodgerblue50, cowboysilver),
  assault_groups
)

assault_base_year <- assaults_indexed |> pull(base_year) |> min()

assault_plot_data <- assaults_indexed |>
  mutate(
    violation = factor(violation, levels = assault_groups),
    hover_id = str_glue("{ucr_code}-{year}"),
    tooltip = str_glue(
      "<b>{violation}</b><br>{year}<br>",
      "Index: {label_number(accuracy = 1)(index)} ({base_year} = 100)<br>",
      "Rate: {label_number(accuracy = 0.1)(incidents_per_100k)} per 100,000"
    )
  )

x_min <- assault_plot_data |> pull(year) |> min()
x_max <- assault_plot_data |> pull(year) |> max()

p <- ggplot(assault_plot_data, aes(x = year, y = index, colour = violation)) +

  # The base line: above it a rate is higher than in the base year.
  geom_hline(yintercept = 100, colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.4) +

  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +

  geom_point_interactive(
    aes(tooltip = tooltip, data_id = hover_id),
    shape = 15, size = 7, alpha = 0
  ) +
  geom_point_interactive(aes(data_id = hover_id), size = 2.5, alpha = 0) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(2000, x_max, 5),
    labels = label_number(big.mark = "", scale = 1, suffix = ""),
    minor_breaks = seq(x_min, x_max, 1),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.05)),
    position = "bottom"
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, NA),
    breaks = seq(0, 300, 50),
    position = "right",
    labels = label_number(big.mark = ",", scale = 1, suffix = ""),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
  ) +

  # A legend in two columns above the panel; one column on phones (below).
  # The key is drawn as a thick line so the colour is easy to match.
  scale_colour_manual(values = assault_colours) +
  guides(
    x = guide_axis(minor.ticks = TRUE),
    colour = guide_legend(ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE, override.aes = list(linewidth = 1.5, alpha = 1, size = 0))
  ) +

  theme(
    axis.text.y.right = element_text(
      size = rel(1),
      hjust = 1.0,
      vjust = -0.5,
      margin = margin(r = 12, l = -20)
    ),
    # "top" reserves room for the legend; theme_cwr()'s default floats it over
    # the panel, where two rows of keys would sit on the lines.
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.justification = "left",
    legend.text = element_text(size = base_size * 0.7, margin = margin(r = 10, l = 4)),
    legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Title: the finding, in one line",
    subtitle = "Subtitle: what is measured, for whom, and when<br>",
    colour = NULL,
    caption = cwr_caption("Statistics Canada Table 35-10-0180-01", credit = TRUE)
  )

cwr_interactive(
  p, "fig-assaults",
  alt = paste0(
    "Line chart of five kinds of assault in Waterloo Region, ", x_min, " to ",
    x_max, ", each shown as an index where its ", assault_base_year,
    " rate per 100,000 people equals 100. Assault with a weapon or causing ",
    "bodily harm rose the most, to a little over twice its ", assault_base_year,
    " rate. Assaults against a peace officer swing widely but ended well above ",
    "theirs. Common assault is close to its ", assault_base_year, " rate, and ",
    "aggravated assault and other assaults ended below theirs."
  ),
  height = 5.5, phone_height = 6,
  phone = list(
    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = seq(2000, x_max, 10),
      minor_breaks = seq(x_min, x_max, 1),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.05))
    ),
    guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 1, override.aes = list(linewidth = 1.5, alpha = 1, size = 0)))
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| label: sexual-offences

# Replicates the Globe and Mail's fourth chart (sexual offence rates for
# Canada, indexed) for Waterloo Region instead. As in the Globe's chart,
# sexual violations against children are indexed to 2015, the others to the
# first year in the data. Legend and hover as in the assault chart.

sexual_groups <- c(
  "Sexual violations against children",
  "Sexual assault with a weapon or causing bodily harm",
  "Sexual assault",
  "Aggravated sexual assault"
)
sexual_colours <- set_names(manual_4_colours, sexual_groups)

# An offence with no incidents in its base year has no index (the data script
# leaves it blank), so it cannot be drawn. It is named in a note instead.
sexual_omitted <- sexual_offences_indexed |>
  summarise(no_index = all(is.na(index)), base_year = first(base_year), .by = violation) |>
  filter(no_index)

sexual_notes <- if (nrow(sexual_omitted) > 0) {
  str_glue(
    "{str_flatten_comma(sexual_omitted$violation, ' and ')} not shown: ",
    "the {cwr_region} recorded none in {str_flatten_comma(unique(sexual_omitted$base_year))}, so there is no base to index to"
  )
}

sexual_plot_data <- sexual_offences_indexed |>
  filter(!is.na(index)) |>
  mutate(
    violation = factor(violation, levels = sexual_groups),
    hover_id = str_glue("{ucr_code}-{year}"),
    tooltip = str_glue(
      "<b>{violation}</b><br>{year}<br>",
      "Index: {label_number(accuracy = 1)(index)} ({base_year} = 100)<br>",
      "Rate: {label_number(accuracy = 0.01)(incidents_per_100k)} per 100,000<br>",
      "Incidents: {label_number(big.mark = ',')(incidents)}"
    )
  )

x_min <- sexual_plot_data |> pull(year) |> min()
x_max <- sexual_plot_data |> pull(year) |> max()

p <- ggplot(sexual_plot_data, aes(x = year, y = index, colour = violation)) +

  geom_hline(yintercept = 100, colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.4) +

  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +

  geom_point_interactive(
    aes(tooltip = tooltip, data_id = hover_id),
    shape = 15, size = 7, alpha = 0
  ) +
  geom_point_interactive(aes(data_id = hover_id), size = 2.5, alpha = 0) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(2000, x_max, 5),
    labels = label_number(big.mark = "", scale = 1, suffix = ""),
    minor_breaks = seq(x_min, x_max, 1),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.05)),
    position = "bottom"
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, NA),
    position = "right",
    labels = label_number(big.mark = ",", scale = 1, suffix = ""),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
  ) +

  scale_colour_manual(values = sexual_colours) +
  guides(
    x = guide_axis(minor.ticks = TRUE),
    colour = guide_legend(ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE, override.aes = list(linewidth = 1.5, alpha = 1, size = 0))
  ) +

  theme(
    axis.text.y.right = element_text(
      size = rel(1),
      hjust = 1.0,
      vjust = -0.5,
      margin = margin(r = 12, l = -20)
    ),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.justification = "left",
    legend.text = element_text(size = base_size * 0.7, margin = margin(r = 10, l = 4)),
    legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Title: the finding, in one line",
    subtitle = "Subtitle: what is measured, for whom, and when<br>",
    colour = NULL,
    caption = cwr_caption("Statistics Canada Table 35-10-0180-01", credit = TRUE, notes = sexual_notes)
  )

cwr_interactive(
  p, "fig-sexual-offences",
  alt = paste0(
    "Line chart of three kinds of sexual offence in Waterloo Region, ", x_min,
    " to ", x_max, ", each shown as an index where its base-year rate per ",
    "100,000 people equals 100 (2015 for sexual violations against children, ",
    x_min, " for the others). Sexual violations against children have about ",
    "tripled since 2015. Sexual assault with a weapon or causing bodily harm is ",
    "about six times its ", x_min, " rate, but it is a handful of incidents a ",
    "year, so the line jumps sharply. Sexual assault is close to its ", x_min,
    " rate. Aggravated sexual assault is not shown because there were none in ",
    x_min, "."
  ),
  height = 5.5, phone_height = 6,
  phone = list(
    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = seq(2000, x_max, 10),
      minor_breaks = seq(x_min, x_max, 1),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.05))
    ),
    guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 1, override.aes = list(linewidth = 1.5, alpha = 1, size = 0)))
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| label: first
#| output: asis

# Pick a template from the cwr-charts skill and build the chart as `p`, then hand
# it to cwr_figure(): it saves a desktop and a phone version of the chart to
# figures/ and writes the figure. Width is fixed at the paragraph width. A
# chart with categories on its y axis (bars, lollipops) needs no height: it is
# worked out so every row is drawn the same depth in every post. Any other chart
# (a line chart, a map) adds `height = 5, phone_height = 4.5` or whatever suits
# it. A Deep dive gets "Figure 1" under the chart and can be
# referred to as @fig-first; a Snapshot gets no label. That follows the post
# type in `categories` above, so there is nothing to set here.
#
# Running this chunk rather than rendering draws both versions to look at, the
# desktop one last, and writes nothing to the post.
p <- ggplot()

cwr_figure(
  p, "fig-first",
  alt = "What the chart shows, for screen readers."
)
```
